newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans down in anticipation of farmer sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans down in anticipation of farmer sales.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures traded lower at midsession as speculators took short positions in anticipation of heavy cash sales in the new year, traders said.
"A lot of our weakness today (Monday) is in anticipation of early-year cash sales," a floor trader said.
Some grain merchandisers said Monday that cash sales of soybeans had picked up over the weekend, and many were looking for more sales after next week.'
Soybean prices were also pressured by expectations of lower demand for soybean meal from U.S. hog producers because the U.S. herd is not growing, traders said.
USDA reported on Friday that the U.S. hog herd was declining at a time when most in the trade were looking for herd expansion.

Weekly export inspections of 25 million bushels from USDA were seen as slightly supportive to the market, traders said. Traders had been looking for exports ranging from 25 to 30 million bushels, trade sources said.
At 1135 CST, soybeans were down 1-1/2 to 5-1/4, with January soybeans down 5-1/4 at $6.96-1/4.
